subject: Short-term residency bridge request and subprocessor roster for pilot
messages:
From: Sarah Bennett <sarah.bennett@hearthhealth.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-09-30T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Residency for pilot: short-term cross-region bridge + subprocessor roster ask

Hi Vanessa,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We're lining up a small EU pilot (subset of patient-facing features) and legal/procurement have a couple of asks before we kick off: 

1) During the pilot we expect occasional operational maintenance in the US region. Can Redwood confirm whether transient cross-region processing/egress for up to 72 hours is covered under your standard DPA or whether we need an addendum? We prefer EU-only processing but need an explicit pathway for short-term failover.

2) Can you share a current subprocessor roster (including EU compute and analytics providers) and a simple statement of whether analytics/telemetry data for the pilot will ever leave the EU?

3) KMS: we want to confirm options for customer-managed keys or escrow for audit purposes. If customer-managed keys aren't available on hosted plans, what controls or evidence can you provide?

4) Audit evidence: procurement asks for sample audit log extract (redacted) and expected retention windows for request/response logs and operational traces.

If possible please attach any DPA addendum draft and subprocessor list — procurement is on a tight timeline. Happy to do a 30m sync today if that helps.

Best,
Sarah
Sarah Bennett
Director, Vendor Risk — Hearth Health
---
From: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Bennett <sarah.bennett@hearthhealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-09-30T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Residency for pilot: short-term cross-region bridge + subprocessor roster ask

Hi Sarah — thanks for the clear asks. I've pulled together the immediate answers and attached a starter DPA addendum and our current subprocessor roster. Quick summary below; attachments are DPA_Addendum_Proposal_v1.pdf and Subprocessor_Roster_Q3_2027.csv.

- Short-term cross-region processing: For hosted customers we operate with EU region preference by default. We support a controlled transient failover window (up to 72 hours) for operational continuity (scheduled maintenance or emergency) provided we follow the notification and approval procedures in the addendum. The proposed addendum (attached) documents the conditions and audit notices; if you need stricter language we can tighten the SLA/certification clauses.

- Telemetry/analytics: Service telemetry (aggregated metrics) is occasionally processed in our analytics cluster in the US for platform health monitoring. For pilot work handling PHI-like data, we propose two controls: 1) field-level filtering to avoid sending PII to analytics, and 2) a temporary analytics hold configured for your account during the pilot. We'll describe both in the addendum.

- KMS: Customer-managed keys are available on Redwood Dedicated and Private deployments. For hosted, we can offer an escrow/escrowed-key-review workflow under an enterprise addendum (we've included suggested language). If you require immediate CMEK on hosted we can discuss a short Dedicated trial.

- Audit logs & retention: Standard request/response logs are retained for 90 days by default; we can extend retention or provide an export snapshot for procurement review. I've linked a sample extract in the Drive folder (redacted).

Next steps I propose:
1) Quick legal + ops call today (30m) to sign off on the addendum language.
2) Procurement to confirm required retention window and any additional telemetry carveouts.
3) If you want CMEK/Dedicated for the pilot we can pull costs and a timeline (2–3 weeks to provision).

I'm looping in Marissa (product ops) to run the technical runbook and provide the bridging playbook.

Cheers,
Vanessa Ortiz
Sr. Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
Attachments: DPA_Addendum_Proposal_v1.pdf (attached), Subprocessor_Roster_Q3_2027.csv (attached)

Vanessa / team — thanks for the quick turnaround and attachments. A few follow-ups before legal will sign the addendum:

We also prefer DocuSign for the addendum execution; procurement will push to legal once the runbook and log-location confirmation are provided.
